about: The accepted-debt ledger. Every entry is a judgement somebody made once, in writing, with a reason, and the gate holds the repository to the count that was agreed. A count that grows fails the gate and names the new line. Nothing here is a permission; it is a record that a specific number of specific hits were looked at on a specific day and found to be what they claim to be.
how_to_use: Do not add an entry to make a failure go away. Read the finding first. Most token hits under the cultural rules are the prohibition being stated or enforced, and those belong here. A hit that is the thing the rule forbids belongs in a deletion, not here.

accepted.reason: The events pack uses the word correctly, in its own notes, to record what has deliberately been left out: the named days within the Quandamooka Festival season, and the absence of any local NAIDOC programme. src/ui/panels/events.js substitutes the word before any of those notes reaches a screen. See docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md G2.

The chronicle's own guard. CEREMONY_TOKENS is the list it greps every published line against, so it has to contain the words in order to refuse them.
The director's matching guard list, and the comment above it.

The substitution table itself. This panel is the reason the word never reaches a screen; it has to name the word to replace it. docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md G2 asks whether substituting is the right call at all.
A comment explaining the difference between a Welcome, which is given by Traditional Owners, and an acknowledgement, which is what this project gives.

The aquifer record's community_concern field and its source, quoting a Redland City Bulletin headline about residents fearing lagoons drying. It reports a published community concern, names no place, carries no coordinate and takes no position. It is the closest thing in the packs to a live question rather than a settled one, and it is named in the wave 8 handover for a cultural reviewer to look at, because it is a word that could reach a player through an ecology readout.

no_accepted_spellings: There is deliberately no australian-english entry here. Every American spelling the check found on 10 August 2026 turned out to be a device meter, behind-the-meter solar, or the Australian Labor Party, so the patterns were narrowed until the check was right rather than the hits accepted. A spelling finding should be fixed, not ledgered.

pointers.reason: The published Australian Bureau of Statistics proportion for the island at the 2021 census. It is an aggregate fact about a place, not a field on a person. The prohibition is about assigning Aboriginality to a simulated resident, and no resident or household in this build carries such a field; see docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md R2. Removing the census figure would falsify the townships, which is the opposite of what the rule protects.

The status field holds a paragraph of legal status rather than a record status: the erosion-prone area declaration and the shoreline erosion management plan. It is accurate prose in the wrong field, so src/world/data.js cannot classify it and the record renders with no marker. The fix belongs to whoever owns the ecology pack: move the paragraph to legal_status and put a classifiable word in status. Held at one so nothing else joins it.
status holds the sentence MODELLED. Not measured. Read the inputs table before using any number here. Same fault as the ecology one: an honest sentence in a field that is supposed to be a word.

status holds a sentence describing a funded concept design with consultation closed. This is the one of the four worth acting on first: it is a real proposal that the runtime cannot tell is a proposal, so it renders without the Proposed marker. Named in the wave 8 handover.

status holds a sentence describing a development partner withdrawing while the priority development area stays in place. Same fault as projects[0], and the same consequence: a proposal with no marker.
